title: POC Rapid Onramp Framework — Gateway Retail
content:
Purpose and brief
---
This doc is a pragmatic, timeboxed onboarding and success framework for the Gateway Retail POC. Goal: validate that Redwood Inference can serve a customer-facing product QA assistant for their product catalog search and returns, meeting latency, cost, and precision thresholds in a 5-week engagement.

High-level objectives
1) Functional: Integrate Redwood hosted API (and one Dedicated fallback) into Gateway's QA assistant prototype to power product search query rewriting and short-form answer generation.
2) Performance: Achieve 95th-percentile latency <= 180ms per token for interactive queries under a simulated peak of 20 rps.
3) Cost: Demonstrate a per-session inference cost <= $0.035 for typical 3-turn flows with cached prefixes.
4) Quality: Maintain precision (answer correctness vs. labelled set) >= 86% on our client-provided evaluation prompts.
5) Operability: Reach a repeatable deploy/runbook and documented rollback plan so Gateway can take over or purchase Dedicated capacity.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope)
- In scope: API integration, sample prompt templates, canonical eval set of ~250 prompts, simple frontend demo, latency and cost profiling, canary rollout plan.
- Out of scope: Full production data sync, complex RBAC audit integrations, custom model training. These can be scoped into follow-up Dedicated engagement.

Deliverables by week
Week 0 (pre-kickoff)
- Signed POC MOU and data access checklist completed. Redwood SRE and Gateway infra contacts added to project channel.

Week 1 (kickoff & baseline)
- Kickoff workshop (90m) covering architecture, required credentials, and success metrics.
- Baseline: run Redwood hosted API with a minimal prompt set, capture baseline latencies and token counts.

Week 2 (integration & eval)
- Implement integration hooks in Gateway staging (API key + sample request handler).
- Build canonical eval harness and run initial quality pass (250 prompts).

Week 3 (load & opt)
- Load testing at increasing concurrency up to 20 rps.
- Apply batching/cache suggestions from Redwood Optimize; test quantized variant if client agrees.

Week 4 (demo & canary)
- Prepare user-facing demo and run stakeholder walkthrough.
- Execute canary route with 5% traffic through Redwood dedicated pool (if available).

Week 5 (wrap & sign-off)
- Produce final report: latency/cost/quality comparisons, recommended config, and runbook.
- Sign-off workshop and acceptance decision.

Roles & primary contacts
- Gateway product lead: Nora Blake (Gateway) — business sign-off
- SE lead (Redwood): Priya Sharma — POC owner, tech lead
- SRE (Redwood): Liam Chen — load and observability
- Solution architect (Gateway): Diego Ramirez — integration owner
- Customer success: Asha Patel — commercial/contracting

Kickoff workshop agenda (90 minutes)
- 0–10m: Introductions & objectives
- 10–25m: Current product flow & integration points (Gateway)
- 25–45m: Redwood architecture overview: hosted vs. dedicated, routing, caching, and failover
- 45–60m: Success metrics and acceptance criteria deep-dive
- 60–80m: Hands-on: run first sample query against hosted API
- 80–90m: Action items, immediate blockers, and next steps

Acceptance criteria (detailed — must be met for POC success)
1) Latency SLOs
- 95th-percentile end-to-end inference latency <= 180ms for interactive queries (measured from Redwood API ingress to first token delivered). Measurement method: synthetic replay of 500 queries representative of production mix during controlled load test.

2) Cost target
- Average per-session inference cost <= $0.035 for a 3-turn session (defined as full token consumption across generation calls). Cost calculation: Redwood billing export for the POC API key and normalization by sessions.

3) Quality thresholds
- Accuracy: >= 86% correctness on the canonical eval set (250 labeled prompts). Labeled by Gateway SMEs.
- Safety: no high-severity hallucinations on 0.5% of prompts (audit sample). Any high-severity outputs must be reproducible and remedied by prompt constraints or model fallback.

4) Reliability & observability
- Successful 2-minute rolling deployment without errors >1% during canary.
- Redwood Console dashboards configured for the POC route, including per-request traces and token-level cost breakdown.

5) Operational handoff readiness
- Documented runbook (deploy, rollback, troubleshooting) and operations onboarding session completed.

Test plan and evaluation approach
- Canonical evaluation harness: pytest-based script that posts prompts, records tokens and latencies, and checks outputs vs. label.
- Synthetic load testing: k6 script to ramp to 20 rps sustained for 10 minutes, with peaks to 30 rps.
- Cost measurement: enable detailed usage logging in Redwood Console and export CSV for accounting.

Data & access requirements (gateway must provide)
- Staging API endpoint for integration testing (no PII), CORS exceptions for demo domain
- Example product catalog CSV (<= 50k rows) and sample user queries (min 500) with labels for 250 evaluation prompts
- Engineering IAM contacts and temporary SSH jump box credentials (if using on-prem components)

Risk register (top 5)
- Missing labeled eval data -> mitigation: Redwood SE will help craft a smaller labeled set (50 prompts) to unblock week 2, and expand later.
- Latency above threshold under load -> mitigation: try smaller sequence lengths, enable KV caching, evaluate Dedicated capacity or region fallback.
- Cost exceeds target -> mitigation: apply quantization suggestions and prefix caching; simulate traffic to fine-tune.
- Unstable demo environment (frontend) -> mitigation: separate simple static demo that calls Redwood directly to isolate infra issues.
- Access delays (credentials/whitelisting) -> mitigation: require access checklist completion before kickoff and escalate via CS.

Sign-off and acceptance process
- Acceptance criteria will be evaluated during Week 5 wrap-up. Gateway product lead and Redwood SE lead must both approve the final report to mark the POC successful. If criteria are partially met, we capture a remediation plan and limited extension proposal.

Appendix: quick checklist for Day 1
- Confluence project created and shared: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/SE/GR-POC-Overview
- API keys provisioned and environment variables shared with Gateway staging team
- Eval dataset uploaded to shared drive and labelled sheet created (column: prompt, label, category)
- Redwood Console route created and basic dashboards visible to Gateway attendees

Notes to self (SE lead)
- Keep prompts short during first demo to avoid long token counts.
- Track any model fallbacks and exact model variants used for reproducibility.
- Capture screenshots of dashboards for final report.

Open questions for kickoff
- Does Gateway want the assistant to cite product SKUs in answers (requires vector store + embedding retrieval)? If yes, add retrieval component to scope.
- Dedicated capacity budget ceilings? This will determine if Dedicated fallback is allowed during canary.

Quick next steps (immediate)
- Schedule kickoff workshop (target: next Tuesday 11/5) — Priya to send invite
- Gateway to share initial 250 prompts and product catalog by 11/4
- Redwood SRE to provision a test route and API key by 11/6
